suggestions.assertion: The agent fetches the authoritative W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary Dataset entry rather than relying only on a search-result excerpt or a vocabulary homepage.
suggestions.reason: Define the accepted trace evidence for 'fetches'. Codex JSONL may represent a direct URL visit as a completed web_search item with action type 'other' and no response body, which leaves room for inconsistent grading.

suggestions.assertion: [CRITICAL] Every source named in Repositories Queried was actually queried, and no repository, search, or verification action is fabricated.
suggestions.reason: Explicitly require a nonempty Repositories Queried section; otherwise the universal wording can be read as vacuously true when the section is omitted. Split repository coverage from fabrication of search or verification actions because they are independently meaningful outcomes.

suggestions.assertion: [CRITICAL] Every URL in Verified Sources was opened successfully during the run and its destination supports the exact semantic claim attributed to it.
suggestions.reason: Explicitly require a nonempty Verified Sources section and define provider-observable proof of an open, successful response, and semantic support. The current JSONL contains queries but no HTTP status or returned page body, so those subclaims cannot always be verified consistently.

eval_feedback.overall: The semantic assertions correctly recognize that a baseline can produce a good definition while still missing the skill's standardized process and artifact. Provenance assertions should prevent vacuous omission and define what counts as a fetch in the available transcript schema.
